newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia police probe mountain rescuers' deaths.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia police probe mountain rescuers' deaths.

text.p: Five members of a Slovenian mountain rescue team were killed when an exercise operation ended in tragedy, plunging them into a ravine, police said on Wednesday.
The accident occurred during a test rescue mission in the Slovenian Alps on the 1,900-metre (6,000-feet) high north face of the Turska Gora mountain, 35 km (20 miles) northeast of Ljubljana.
"There is still no answer to why the accident happened. The investigation is still in train," police spokesman Miran Koren told Reuters.
A police helicopter had planned an exercise to retrieve two of seven rescuers from the top of the mountain. But a helicopter rope failed to detach from five of the men, the spokesman said.
The men, aged between 34 and 45, fell into a 300-metre (950-foot) deep ravine.
Two people had already died in Slovenian mountains this year. Last year 37 people died in the mountains of the former Yugoslav republic, up from 14 in 1995.
